summary: The v3 case stops at step 4 when the Tourist applies inventory letter f, a tripe ration (object 264). C apply.c doapply() reaches its default arm: the ration is neither a pole weapon, pick, nor axe, so C prints “Sorry, I don’t know how to use that.” and returns ECMD_FAIL without a turn. JS already implements that result for carrots and ordinary armor but refuses this food object. Extend the source default decision across the safe object class, while preserving named arms and the banana hallucination branch.

source.branch: A sighted Tourist selects a carried tripe ration for the a/apply command on dungeon level 1. After selection, the object bypasses all named doapply() switch arms and reaches the default arm; is_pole, is_pick, and is_axe are false, so C prints the unknown-use message and returns ECMD_FAIL.
callers: cmd.c a/apply dispatch reaches apply.c doapply(); js/cmd.js runApplyCommand() calls js/apply.js doapply() through failClosedCommand().
dependencies: C default at apply.c:4405-4417 redirects pole weapons to use_pole and picks or axes to use_pick_axe before the unknown-use message. Preserve those return-valued branches as refusals until their functions are ported.
BANANA has a preceding named arm with a Hallucination-specific message and falls through to default only otherwise; preserve that source condition when extending the ordinary food result.
